sanskrit: sa saṃjñām upalabhyātha bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān nivārayām āsa tadā svāny anīkāni māriṣa
english: Then, regaining his senses, the valiant son of Bharadvāja held back his own divisions at that moment, O honored one.

sanskrit: vinivṛttān kurūn dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavāpi svasainikān dūtaiḥ śīghrāśvasaṃyuktair avahāram akārayan
english: Seeing the Kurus withdraw, the Pāṇḍavas too, through messengers mounted on swift horses, caused their own troops to retire from the field.

sanskrit: vinivṛtteṣu sainyeṣu pāraṃparyeṇa sarvaśaḥ vimuktakavacāḥ sarve bhīṣmam īyur narādhipāḥ
english: When the armies had everywhere withdrawn in succession, all the kings, their armor laid aside, went to Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: vyupāramya tato yuddhād yodhāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ upatasthur mahātmānaṃ prajāpatim ivāmarāḥ
english: Then, ceasing from battle, the warriors in their hundreds of thousands stood attending upon that great-souled one, as the immortals attend Prajāpati.

sanskrit: te tu bhīṣmaṃ samāsādya śayānaṃ bharatarṣabham abhivādya vyatiṣṭhanta pāṇḍavāḥ kurubhiḥ saha
english: Approaching Bhīṣma, that bull of the Bharatas, as he lay there, the Pāṇḍavas together with the Kurus paid him homage and took their places around him.

sanskrit: atha pāṇḍūn kurūṃś caiva praṇipatyāgrataḥ sthitān abhyabhāṣata dharmātmā bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavas tadā
english: Then to the Pāṇḍavas and the Kurus, who stood bowing before him, the righteous Bhīṣma, son of Śantanu, spoke.

sanskrit: svāgataṃ vo mahābhāgāḥ svāgataṃ vo mahārathāḥ tuṣyāmi darśanāc cāhaṃ yuṣmākam amaropamāḥ
english: "Welcome to you, illustrious ones; welcome to you, great chariot-warriors. I rejoice at the sight of you, who are like the immortals."

sanskrit: abhinandya sa tān evaṃ śirasā lambatābravīt śiro me lambate 'tyartham upadhānaṃ pradīyatām
english: Having greeted them thus, with his head hanging down he said: "My head hangs too low; let a pillow be given to me."

sanskrit: tato nṛpāḥ samājahrus tanūni ca mṛdūni ca upadhānāni mukhyāni naicchat tāni pitāmahaḥ
english: Then the kings brought choice pillows, thin and soft; but the grandsire would not have them.

sanskrit: abravīc ca naravyāghraḥ prahasann iva tān nṛpān naitāni vīraśayyāsu yuktarūpāṇi pārthivāḥ
english: And that tiger among men said to those kings, as if smiling: "These, O princes, are not fitting for a hero's bed."

sanskrit: tato vīkṣya naraśreṣṭham abhyabhāṣata pāṇḍavam dhanaṃjayaṃ dīrghabāhuṃ sarvalokamahāratham
english: Then, looking upon that best of men, the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya, the long-armed great chariot-warrior of all the worlds, he addressed him.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjaya mahābāho śiraso me 'sya lambataḥ dīyatām upadhānaṃ vai yad yuktam iha manyase
english: "O Dhanaṃjaya, mighty-armed, this head of mine hangs down; let such a pillow be given as you here deem fitting."

sanskrit: sa saṃnyasya mahac cāpam abhivādya pitāmaham netrābhyām aśrupūrṇābhyām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Setting aside his great bow and saluting the grandsire, with his two eyes brimming with tears he spoke these words.

sanskrit: ājñāpaya kuruśreṣṭha sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ vara preṣyo 'haṃ tava durdharṣa kriyatāṃ kiṃ pitāmaha
english: "Command me, O best of the Kurus, foremost of all wielders of weapons. I am your servant, O unassailable one; what shall be done, grandsire?"

sanskrit: tam abravīc chāṃtanavaḥ śiro me tāta lambate upadhānaṃ kuruśreṣṭha phalgunopanayasva me śayanasyānurūpaṃ hi śīghraṃ vīra prayaccha me
english: The son of Śantanu said to him: "My head hangs down, my son. O best of the Kurus, Phalguna, fetch me a pillow; quickly, O hero, give me one befitting this bed of mine."

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi pārtha mahābāho śreṣṭhaḥ sarvadhanuṣmatām kṣatradharmasya vettā ca buddhisattvaguṇānvitaḥ
english: "For you, O Pārtha, mighty-armed, are the foremost of all bowmen, knower of the kṣatriya's law, endowed with the virtues of wisdom and resolve."

sanskrit: phalgunas tu tathety uktvā vyavasāyapurojavaḥ pragṛhyāmantrya gāṇḍīvaṃ śarāṃś ca nataparvaṇaḥ
english: Phalguna, saying "So be it," swift and forward in resolve, took up the Gāṇḍīva and, with sacred utterance, his keen-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: anumānya mahātmānaṃ bharatānām amadhyamam tribhis tīkṣṇair mahāvegair udagṛhṇāc chiraḥ śaraiḥ
english: Having sought the leave of that great-souled, peerless one among the Bharatas, with three sharp, swift-flying arrows he upheld his head.

sanskrit: abhiprāye tu vidite dharmātmā savyasācinā atuṣyad bharataśreṣṭho bhīṣmo dharmārthatattvavit
english: When his intent was understood by Savyasācin, the righteous one, Bhīṣma, that best of the Bharatas, knower of the truths of dharma and artha, was well pleased.

sanskrit: upadhānena dattena pratyanandad dhanaṃjayam kuntīputraṃ yudhāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ suhṛdāṃ prītivardhanam
english: With the pillow thus given, he praised Dhanaṃjaya, the son of Kuntī, the best of fighters, the increaser of his friends' delight.

sanskrit: anurūpaṃ śayānasya pāṇḍavopahitaṃ tvayā yady anyathā pravartethāḥ śapeyaṃ tvām ahaṃ ruṣā
english: "O Pāṇḍava, you have provided what befits one who lies thus. Had you acted otherwise, I would have cursed you in my wrath."

sanskrit: evam etan mahābāho dharmeṣu pariniṣṭhitam svaptavyaṃ kṣatriyeṇājau śaratalpagatena vai
english: "This is so, O mighty-armed one, established firmly in the laws: thus must a kṣatriya sleep in battle, lying upon a bed of arrows."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu bībhatsuṃ sarvāṃs tān abravīd vacaḥ rājñaś ca rājaputrāṃś ca pāṇḍavenābhi saṃsthitān
english: Having spoken thus to Bībhatsu, he addressed these words to all those kings and princes who stood gathered with the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: śayeyam asyāṃ śayyāyāṃ yāvad āvartanaṃ raveḥ ye tadā pārayiṣyanti te māṃ drakṣyanti vai nṛpāḥ
english: "I shall lie upon this bed until the sun turns back in its course. Those kings who shall then survive will indeed behold me."

sanskrit: diśaṃ vaiśravaṇākrāntāṃ yadā gantā divākaraḥ arciṣmān pratapaṃl lokān rathenottamatejasā vimokṣye 'haṃ tadā prāṇān suhṛdaḥ supriyān api
english: "When the sun, the day-maker, blazing and scorching the worlds with his chariot of supreme splendor, shall pass to the quarter ruled by Vaiśravaṇa, then shall I release my life-breaths, dear though my friends be to me."

sanskrit: parikhā khanyatām atra mamāvasadane nṛpāḥ upāsiṣye vivasvantam evaṃ śaraśatācitaḥ upāramadhvaṃ saṃgrāmād vairāṇy utsṛjya pārthivāḥ
english: "Let a trench be dug here, O kings, around my dwelling-place; thus pierced by a hundred arrows, I shall worship Vivasvat. Desist from battle, O princes, and cast off your enmities."

sanskrit: upātiṣṭhann atho vaidyāḥ śalyoddharaṇakovidāḥ sarvopakaraṇair yuktāḥ kuśalās te suśikṣitāḥ
english: Then physicians came near, skilled in the drawing-out of arrows, furnished with all their instruments, expert and well-trained.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā jāhnavīputraḥ provāca vacanaṃ tadā dattadeyā visṛjyantāṃ pūjayitvā cikitsakāḥ
english: Seeing them, the son of Jāhnavī then spoke these words: "Let the physicians be honored, given their due, and dismissed."

sanskrit: evaṃgate na hīdānīṃ vaidyaiḥ kāryam ihāsti me kṣatradharmapraśastāṃ hi prāpto 'smi paramāṃ gatim
english: "In this pass there is now no need of physicians for me, for I have attained the supreme goal, lauded by the kṣatriya's law."

sanskrit: naiṣa dharmo mahīpālāḥ śaratalpagatasya me etair eva śaraiś cāhaṃ dagdhavyo 'nte narādhipāḥ
english: "This is not the way, O guardians of the earth, for me who lie upon a bed of arrows; with these very arrows, O kings, I must be burned at the end."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya putro duryodhanas tava vaidyān visarjayām āsa pūjayitvā yathārhataḥ
english: Hearing those words of his, your son Duryodhana dismissed the physicians, having honored them as they deserved.

sanskrit: tatas te vismayaṃ jagmur nānājanapadeśvarāḥ sthitiṃ dharme parāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīṣmasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: Then the lords of diverse realms were filled with wonder, beholding the supreme steadfastness in dharma of Bhīṣma of boundless splendor.

sanskrit: upadhānaṃ tato dattvā pitus tava janeśvara sahitāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ sarve kuravaś ca mahārathāḥ
english: Then, having given a pillow to your father, O lord of men, all the Pāṇḍavas together and the Kuru great chariot-warriors—

sanskrit: upagamya mahātmānaṃ śayānaṃ śayane śubhe te 'bhivādya tato bhīṣmaṃ kṛtvā cābhipradakṣiṇam
english: —approaching that great-souled one as he lay upon his auspicious bed, saluted Bhīṣma and circled him with reverence.

sanskrit: vidhāya rakṣāṃ bhīṣmasya sarva eva samantataḥ vīrāḥ svaśibirāṇy eva dhyāyantaḥ paramāturāḥ niveśāyābhyupāgacchan sāyāhne rudhirokṣitāḥ
english: Having set guards about Bhīṣma on every side, all those heroes, deep in thought and sorely grieved, went toward their own camps at evening to take their rest, drenched in blood.

sanskrit: niviṣṭān pāṇḍavāṃś cāpi prīyamāṇān mahārathān bhīṣmasya patanād dhṛṣṭān upagamya mahārathān uvāca yādavaḥ kāle dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: And to the Pāṇḍava great chariot-warriors, encamped and rejoicing, gladdened by the fall of Bhīṣma, the Yādava drew near at the fit time and spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā jayasi kauravya diṣṭyā bhīṣmo nipātitaḥ avadhyo mānuṣair eṣa satyasaṃdho mahārathaḥ
english: "By good fortune you triumph, O Kaurava; by good fortune Bhīṣma is laid low—he, the great chariot-warrior, true to his word, unslayable by mortals."

sanskrit: atha vā daivataiḥ pārtha sarvaśastrāstrapāragaḥ tvāṃ tu cakṣurhaṇaṃ prāpya dagdho ghoreṇa cakṣuṣā
english: "Or rather, O Pārtha, he who was master of all weapons and missiles, even by the gods could not be slain—but, encountering you whose very glance destroys, he was consumed by your terrible eye."

sanskrit: evam ukto dharmarājaḥ pratyuvāca janārdanam tava prasādād vijayaḥ krodhāt tava parājayaḥ tvaṃ hi naḥ śaraṇaṃ kṛṣṇa bhaktānām abhayaṃkaraḥ
english: Thus addressed, the King of Righteousness replied to Janārdana: "Through your grace comes victory, through your wrath comes defeat. For you, O Kṛṣṇa, are our refuge, the giver of fearlessness to your devotees."

sanskrit: anāścaryo jayas teṣāṃ yeṣāṃ tvam asi keśava raṣkitā samare nityaṃ nityaṃ cāpi hite rataḥ sarvathā tvāṃ samāsādya nāścaryam iti me matiḥ
english: "No wonder is victory for those whose protector in battle you ever are, O Keśava, ever devoted to their good. Having gained you in every way, that there should be no wonder—such is my conviction."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca smayamāno janārdanaḥ tvayy evaitad yuktarūpaṃ vacanaṃ pārthivottama
english: Thus addressed, Janārdana replied, smiling: "This speech befits none but you, O best of kings."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vyuṣṭāyāṃ tu mahārāja rajanyāṃ sarvapārthivāḥ pāṇḍavā dhārtarāṣṭrāś ca abhijagmuḥ pitāmaham
english: Saṃjaya said: When the night had passed, O great king, all the princes—the Pāṇḍavas and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra—went forth to the grandsire.

sanskrit: taṃ vīraśayane vīraṃ śayānaṃ kurusattamam abhivādyopatasthur vai kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriyarṣabham
english: That hero, best of the Kurus, as he lay upon his hero's bed, the kṣatriyas saluted and attended upon, that bull among kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: kanyāś candanacūrṇaiś ca lājair mālyaiś ca sarvaśaḥ striyo bālās tathā vṛddhāḥ prekṣakāś ca pṛthagjanāḥ samabhyayuḥ śāṃtanavaṃ bhūtānīva tamonudam
english: Maidens with sandal-powder and parched grain and garlands on every side, women, children, and the aged, and onlookers of the common folk, drew near the son of Śantanu as living beings draw near the dispeller of darkness.

sanskrit: tūryāṇi gaṇikā vārās tathaiva naṭanartakāḥ upānṛtyañ jaguś caiva vṛddhaṃ kurupitāmaham
english: Musicians, courtesans, and likewise actors and dancers danced and sang before the aged grandsire of the Kurus.

sanskrit: upāramya ca yuddhebhyaḥ saṃnāhān vipramucya ca āyudhāni ca nikṣipya sahitāḥ kurupāṇḍavāḥ
english: Ceasing from their battles, loosing off their armor, and laying down their weapons, the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas together—

sanskrit: anvāsata durādharṣaṃ devavratam ariṃdamam anyonyaṃ prītimantas te yathāpūrvaṃ yathāvayaḥ
english: —sat attending upon the unassailable Devavrata, that subduer of foes, affectionate toward one another as before, each according to his age.

sanskrit: sā pārthivaśatākīrṇā samitir bhīṣmaśobhitā śuśubhe bhāratī dīptā divīvādityamaṇḍalam
english: That assembly of the Bharatas, thronged with a hundred princes and graced by Bhīṣma, shone resplendent like the orb of the sun blazing in the sky.

sanskrit: vibabhau ca nṛpāṇāṃ sā pitāmaham upāsatām devānām iva deveśaṃ pitāmaham upāsatām
english: And that gathering of kings waiting upon the grandsire shone forth like the gods waiting upon the lord of gods, the Grandsire of all.

sanskrit: bhīṣmas tu vedanāṃ dhairyān nigṛhya bharatarṣabha abhitaptaḥ śaraiś caiva nātihṛṣṭamanābravīt
english: But Bhīṣma, O bull of the Bharatas, mastering his pain through fortitude, sore-tormented by the arrows, spoke with a mind not over-glad.

sanskrit: śarābhitaptakāyo 'haṃ śarasaṃtāpamūrchitaḥ pānīyam abhikāṅkṣe 'haṃ rājñas tān pratyabhāṣata
english: "My body is scorched by the arrows, and I swoon with the burning of their wounds; I long for water"—thus he spoke to those kings.

sanskrit: tatas te kṣatriyā rājan samājahruḥ samantataḥ bhakṣyān uccāvacāṃs tatra vārikumbhāṃś ca śītalān
english: Then those kṣatriyas, O king, brought from all around foods of every kind and jars of cool water.

sanskrit: upanītaṃ ca tad dṛṣṭvā bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo 'bravīt nādya tāta mayā śakyaṃ bhogān kāṃś cana mānuṣān
english: Seeing what was brought, Bhīṣma, son of Śantanu, said: "It is not possible for me now, my son, to take any human enjoyments."

sanskrit: upabhoktuṃ manuṣyebhyaḥ śaraśayyāgato hy aham pratīkṣamāṇas tiṣṭhāmi nivṛttiṃ śaśisūryayoḥ
english: "For I, removed from men and come to a bed of arrows, remain awaiting the turning-back of the moon and the sun."

sanskrit: evam uktvā śāṃtanavo dīnavāk sarvapārthivān dhanaṃjayaṃ mahābāhum abhyabhāṣata bhārata
english: Having spoken thus to all the princes in a feeble voice, the son of Śantanu addressed the mighty-armed Dhanaṃjaya, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: athopetya mahābāhur abhivādya pitāmaham atiṣṭhat prāñjaliḥ prahvaḥ kiṃ karomīti cābravīt
english: Then the mighty-armed one, approaching and saluting the grandsire, stood with joined palms, bowing, and said: "What shall I do?"

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavaṃ rājann abhivādyāgrataḥ sthitam abhyabhāṣata dharmātmā bhīṣmaḥ prīto dhanaṃjayam
english: Seeing that Pāṇḍava, O king, standing before him with salutation, the righteous Bhīṣma, well pleased, addressed Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: dahyate 'daḥ śarīraṃ me saṃsyūto 'smi maheṣubhiḥ marmāṇi paridūyante vadanaṃ mama śuṣyati
english: "This body of mine burns; I am pierced through and through by great arrows; my vital points are aflame, and my mouth runs dry."

sanskrit: hlādanārthaṃ śarīrasya prayacchāpo mamārjuna tvaṃ hi śakto maheṣvāsa dātum ambho yathāvidhi
english: "To cool my body, give me water, O Arjuna; for you, great archer, are able to bring forth water in the proper way."

sanskrit: arjunas tu tathety uktvā ratham āruhya vīryavān adhijyaṃ balavat kṛtvā gāṇḍīvaṃ vyākṣipad dhanuḥ
english: Arjuna, saying "So be it," the valiant one, mounted his chariot and, drawing the Gāṇḍīva mightily to the string, twanged the bow.

sanskrit: tasya jyātalanirghoṣaṃ visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ vitresuḥ sarvabhūtāni śrutvā sarve ca pārthivāḥ
english: At the sound of his bowstring and palm-guard, like the crashing of a thunderbolt, all beings, hearing it, trembled, and so did all the kings.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā rathena rathināṃ varaḥ śayānaṃ bharataśreṣṭhaṃ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam
english: Then that best of charioteers, having circled in his chariot that best of the Bharatas, foremost of all wielders of weapons, as he lay there—

sanskrit: saṃdhāya ca śaraṃ dīptam abhimantrya mahāyaśāḥ parjanyāstreṇa saṃyojya sarvalokasya paśyataḥ avidhyat pṛthivīṃ pārthaḥ pārśve bhīṣmasya dakṣiṇe
english: —and fixing a blazing arrow, consecrating it with sacred utterance, the illustrious Pārtha joined it to the Parjanya weapon and, before the eyes of all the world, pierced the earth at Bhīṣma's right side.

sanskrit: utpapāta tato dhārā vimalā vāriṇaḥ śivā śītasyāmṛtakalpasya divyagandharasasya ca
english: Thereupon there sprang up a pure and blessed jet of water, cool and like ambrosia, of divine fragrance and savor.

sanskrit: atarpayat tataḥ pārthaḥ śītayā vāridhārayā bhīṣmaṃ kurūṇām ṛṣabhaṃ divyakarmaparākramaḥ
english: Then Pārtha, of divine deeds and prowess, refreshed with that cool jet of water Bhīṣma, the bull of the Kurus.

sanskrit: karmaṇā tena pārthasya śakraṣyeva vikurvataḥ vismayaṃ paramaṃ jagmus tatas te vasudhādhipāḥ
english: At that deed of Pārtha, who wrought wonders like Śakra himself, the lords of the earth then fell into the utmost amazement.

sanskrit: tat karma prekṣya bībhatsor atimānuṣam adbhutam saṃprāvepanta kuravo gāvaḥ śītārditā iva
english: Beholding that superhuman and marvelous deed of Bībhatsu, the Kurus shook all over, like cattle tormented by cold.

sanskrit: vismayāc cottarīyāṇi vyāvidhyan sarvato nṛpāḥ śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣais tumulaṃ sarvato 'bhavat
english: In their wonder the kings waved their upper garments on every side, and with the blare of conches and kettledrums a tumult arose all around.

sanskrit: tṛptaḥ śāṃtanavaś cāpi rājan bībhatsum abravīt sarvapārthivavīrāṇāṃ saṃnidhau pūjayann iva
english: And the son of Śantanu, his thirst quenched, O king, spoke to Bībhatsu in the presence of all the princely heroes, as if honoring him.

sanskrit: naitac citraṃ mahābāho tvayi kauravanandana kathito nāradenāsi pūrvarṣir amitadyutiḥ
english: "This is no marvel in you, O mighty-armed delight of the Kurus; by Nārada you were declared to be an ancient seer of boundless luster."

sanskrit: vāsudevasahāyas tvaṃ mahat karma kariṣyasi yan notsahati devendraḥ saha devair api dhruvam
english: "With Vāsudeva as your ally, you shall accomplish a mighty deed that even Indra, lord of the gods, together with the gods, surely could not dare."

sanskrit: vidus tvāṃ nidhanaṃ pārtha sarvakṣatrasya tadvidaḥ dhanurdharāṇām ekas tvaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pravaro nṛṣu
english: "Those who know such things know you, O Pārtha, to be the destroyer of all the kṣatriya race; alone among bowmen, you are the foremost of men upon the earth."

sanskrit: manuṣyā jagati śreṣṭhāḥ pakṣiṇāṃ garuḍo varaḥ sarasāṃ sāgaraḥ śreṣṭho gaur variṣṭhā catuṣpadām
english: "Among the creatures of the world men are the best; of birds Garuḍa is supreme; of waters the ocean is best; of four-footed beasts the cow is highest."

sanskrit: ādityas tejasāṃ śreṣṭho girīṇāṃ himavān varaḥ jātīnāṃ brāhmaṇaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhas tvam asi dhanvinām
english: "The sun is best of the radiant ones, Himavat the highest of mountains, the brāhmaṇa the best of castes—and you are the best of bowmen."

sanskrit: na vai śrutaṃ dhārtarāṣṭreṇa vākyaṃ; saṃbodhyamānaṃ vidureṇa caiva droṇena rāmeṇa janārdanena; muhur muhuḥ saṃjayenāpi coktam
english: "The counsel given by Vidura was not heeded by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, nor that of Droṇa and Rāma and Janārdana, urged again and again, and spoken too by Saṃjaya."

sanskrit: parītabuddhir hi visaṃjñakalpo; duryodhano nābhyanandad vaco me sa śeṣyate vai nihataś cirāya; śāstrātigo bhīmabalābhibhūtaḥ
english: "For Duryodhana, his mind deranged and well-nigh senseless, took no joy in my words; transgressor of the scriptures, struck down by Bhīma's might, he shall lie slain for ages to come."

sanskrit: tataḥ śrutvā tad vacaḥ kauravendro; duryodhano dīnamanā babhūva tam abravīc chāṃtanavo 'bhivīkṣya; nibodha rājan bhava vītamanyuḥ
english: Then, hearing those words, the lord of the Kurus, Duryodhana, became dejected in heart; and the son of Śantanu, looking upon him, said: "Hear me, O king, and let your anger pass."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭaṃ duryodhanedaṃ te yathā pārthena dhīmatā jalasya dhārā janitā śītasyāmṛtagandhinaḥ etasya kartā loke 'smin nānyaḥ kaś cana vidyate
english: "You have seen, Duryodhana, how by the wise Pārtha this jet of cool water, fragrant as ambrosia, was brought forth; of such a deed there is none other in this world who can be the doer."

sanskrit: āgneyaṃ vāruṇaṃ saumyaṃ vāyavyam atha vaiṣṇavam aindraṃ pāśupataṃ brāhmaṃ pārameṣṭhyaṃ prajāpateḥ dhātus tvaṣṭuś ca savitur divyāny astrāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: "The weapons of Agni, of Varuṇa, of Soma, of Vāyu, and then of Viṣṇu, of Indra, of Paśupati, of Brahmā, of Parameṣṭhin and Prajāpati, of Dhātṛ, of Tvaṣṭṛ, and of Savitṛ—all the divine missiles—"

sanskrit: sarvasmin mānuṣe loke vetty eko hi dhanaṃjayaḥ kṛṣṇo vā devakīputro nānyo vai veda kaś cana na śakyāḥ pāṇḍavās tāta yuddhe jetuṃ kathaṃ cana
english: "In all the world of men, Dhanaṃjaya alone knows them, or Kṛṣṇa the son of Devakī—no other knows them at all. The Pāṇḍavas, my son, cannot in any wise be conquered in battle."
